lines.trans: Vitya, I do not understand you at all today.
For what sake did you stage this whole performance?
Just to flatter your own pride?
And what was I supposed to do with him?
You should have simply told him the truth.
Say that I am just a regular cook here now?
Yes, at least tell that simple truth.
Fine, I will go right now and tell him everything!
Vitya, I see things are going well for you!
Volodya, that is just what I wanted to tell you about.
In fact I am not the head chef here at all...

examples.trans: Wait, you want to come in the evening for dinner?

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (root 'сказать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to tell', forming an aspectual pair with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Володя, вот об этом я хотел рассказать.
examples.trans: Volodya, that is just what I wanted to tell you about.

examples.text: Расскажи, что случилось.
examples.trans: Tell me what happened.

examples.text: Я всё расскажу маме.
examples.trans: I'll tell Mum everything.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Смотри только не пережарь их на сковороде.
examples.trans: Just make sure you do not overcook them in the pan.

examples.text: Лёва, сегодня на обед придут мои гости.
examples.trans: Lyova, my guests will come for lunch today.

examples.text: Подожди, этот сеанс назначен уже на сегодня?
examples.trans: Wait, is this session scheduled for today already?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'the most', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Это же самый лучший сомелье всей Москвы!
examples.trans: That is the very best sommelier in all of Moscow!

examples.text: Самое главное — это народ.
examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.

examples.text: Это самый большой город.
examples.trans: It's the biggest town.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.text: И где ты теперь работаешь главным шефом?
examples.trans: And where are you working as head chef now?

examples.text: Они обязательно попросят к столику главного шефа.
examples.trans: They will definitely ask for the head chef at their table.

examples.text: Стоило хорошему шефу уйти, ягнёнок уже не тот.
examples.trans: As soon as a good chef left, the lamb is not the same.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (root 'винить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to excuse', forming an aspectual pair with 'извинять'.

examples.text: Извини меня, Лена, я сейчас быстро вернусь.
examples.trans: Excuse me, Lena, I will be right back.

examples.text: Лена, извини, мне нужно ещё раз отлучиться.
examples.trans: Lena, excuse me, I need to step away one more time.

examples.text: Извините, давайте мы приготовим вам что-то другое.
examples.trans: Excuse us, let's prepare something else for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Как же вы так меня подводите, друзья?
examples.trans: How can you let me down like that, folks?

examples.text: Вы меня сейчас просто очень сильно расстроили.
examples.trans: You have just upset me very much right now.

examples.text: Я так старался вас сегодня вкусно удивить.
examples.trans: I tried so hard to surprise you deliciously today.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'by chance'.

examples.text: У него в баре случайно сломался замок.
examples.trans: A lock accidentally broke at his bar.

examples.text: Шеф, извините, вы случайно обронили на кухне платок.
examples.trans: Chef, excuse me, you accidentally dropped your handkerchief in the kitchen.

examples.text: А вы случайно не Самсон?
examples.trans: Are you by any chance Samson?

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (root 'ронить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to handkerchief'.

examples.text: Шеф, извините, вы случайно обронили на кухне платок.
examples.trans: Chef, excuse me, you accidentally dropped your handkerchief in the kitchen.

examples.text: Витя, я тебя сегодня совсем не понимаю.
examples.trans: Vitya, I do not understand you at all today.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.text: Сегодня вечером на кухне не будет Германа.
examples.trans: Tonight German will not be in the kitchen.

examples.text: Шеф, извините, вы случайно обронили на кухне платок.
examples.trans: Chef, excuse me, you accidentally dropped your handkerchief in the kitchen.

examples.text: Мы сидим на кухне.
examples.trans: We're sitting in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'kitchen', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Шеф, извините, вы случайно обронили на кухне платок.
examples.trans: Chef, excuse me, you accidentally dropped your handkerchief in the kitchen.

examples.text: Витя, я тебя сегодня совсем не понимаю.
examples.trans: Vitya, I do not understand you at all today.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian interj meaning 'thank you', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, Луи, ты мне очень помог!
examples.trans: Thank you, Louis, you helped me a lot!

examples.text: Ну ладно, спасибо, просто это очень неожиданно.
examples.trans: Well all right, thank you, it is just very unexpected.

examples.text: Спасибо вам большое, друзья, я пошёл в зал.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, pals, I am heading to the hall.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'big', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Они аккуратно стоят в моём большом холодильнике.
examples.trans: They are sitting neatly in my big refrigerator.

examples.text: Спасибо вам большое, друзья, я пошёл в зал.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, pals, I am heading to the hall.

examples.text: Спасибо большое, Елена Павловна.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, Elena Pavlovna.
